post.description:
Validates the signup token (from email verification) and sets the user's password.
Returns auth tokens for auto-login.

# Errors

Returns an error if:
- The signup token is invalid or expired
- The email doesn't match the token
- The user already has a password
- Password hashing fails

400.description: Invalid request or password already set

post.description: Returns an error if service errors occur. Always returns success to prevent email enumeration.

200.description: Reset code sent if email exists

post.summary:
Login with email and password
# Errors
post.description: Returns an error if login fails due to invalid credentials, validation errors, or service errors.

get.description: Returns an error if the user is not found or service errors occur.

post.summary:
Store the browser-generated OAuth device binding in an `HttpOnly` scoped cookie.
# Errors
post.description: Returns an error if the fingerprint contains invalid cookie characters.

get.summary:
Start OAuth flow - redirect to provider.
# Errors
get.description: Returns an error if the provider is invalid, authentication is required but not provided, or service errors occur.

Handles both real OAuth flow and test bypass mode. Always answers with a
redirect: the browser arrives here by top-level navigation from the
provider, so a JSON error body would strand the user on a raw error page.
Provider-reported errors (e.g. a cancelled consent) and every internal
failure go back to `/login` with a fixed error code; the cause is logged,
never put in the URL.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Error reported by the provider, e.g. access_denied

307.description: Redirect to the app with the result, or to /login?error=oauth_cancelled|oauth_failed

delete.summary:
Unlink OAuth provider from account.
# Errors
delete.description: Returns an error if the provider is invalid, not linked, or unlinking fails.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session has expired

post.summary:
Refresh the JWT access token using a refresh token
# Errors
post.description: Returns an error if the refresh token is missing, invalid, expired, or service errors occur.

This is step 1 of the email-first signup flow:
1. User provides email → verification code sent (this endpoint)
2. User verifies email → signup token issued
3. User sets password using signup token → account complete
# Errors

Returns an error if registration fails due to validation, duplicate email, or service errors.

200.description: Verification code sent; for an email that already has an account, its owner is notified instead (same response, so registration can't be used to check for accounts)

502.description: The verification email could not be delivered; the code was not sent, and resending is available immediately

200.description: Same response whether or not a code was sent (unknown email, already verified, cooldown, and lock are not distinguished)

post.description:
Returns auth tokens for auto-login if device fingerprint is provided.
# Errors

Returns an error if the reset token is invalid, expired, missing device fingerprint, or service errors occur.

For new signups (no password yet): Returns a `signup_token` (30 min expiry) to complete signup.
For existing users with password: Returns auth tokens for auto-login.

400.description: Invalid, expired or locked code, email already verified, or a malformed request

get.summary: Legacy magic-link entry point: redirect to the frontend confirmation page.
get.description:
Emails used to link here directly, and this GET verified the email on the
spot. Mail scanners that prefetch links used the token up before the user
clicked, so it no longer has side effects: it only forwards the token, in the
URL fragment, to `/verify-magic`, where the user confirms with a button
(`POST /api/v1/auth/verify-magic`). Kept so links in emails sent before the
change still work; new emails link to the frontend page directly.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The magic link token from the email

303.description: Redirects to the /verify-magic confirmation page with the token in the fragment

post.summary: Confirm a magic link (backup to the 6-digit code).
post.description:
Answers exactly like `verify-email`: a `signup_token` in the body when the
account has no password yet, otherwise a session (cookies) for auto-login.
Nothing here goes into a URL, so the signup token never reaches browser
history or access logs.

400.description: Invalid, expired or locked link, the account is already verified and has a password, or a malformed request

post.summary:

post.description: Returns an error if the code is invalid, expired, or service errors occur.

AuthResponse.description:
Response body for successful authentication and for token refresh.

The JWT access token and refresh token are delivered exclusively as
`HttpOnly` cookies (the native-client body-token path was removed), so only
the non-secret session metadata is returned in the body. Login and refresh
return the identical shape, so they share this one DTO rather than a
duplicate `RefreshResponse`.

csrf_token.description: CSRF token for state-changing requests (also set as a readable cookie).

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp when the access token expires.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: Request to change password (for users who already have a password).

CompleteRegistrationRequest.description:
Request body for completing registration (set password after email verification).

This is step 3 of signup: user sets password after verifying email.

email.description: Email address (for password manager autofill, verified against token).

signup_token.description: The signup completion token from verify-email endpoint (30 min expiry).

message.description:

turnstile_token.description: Cloudflare Turnstile token for bot protection.

This is step 1 of signup: user provides email, we send verification code.
Password is set later after email verification.

Error codes for verification-related errors.
These allow the frontend to show appropriate UI for each error type.

cooldown_seconds.description: For `COOLDOWN_ACTIVE`: seconds until resend is allowed.

email.description: For `SIGNUP_INCOMPLETE`: the email address to continue signup.

VerificationOrStandardError.description:
A `400` from a verification route: either the structured verification error
(wrong, expired or locked code) or, for a malformed request, the standard

VerifyEmailResponse.description:
Response body for email verification during signup.

New users (no password yet) receive a `signup_token` to complete signup.
Existing users with a password are logged in via `HttpOnly` cookies (the
body-token path was removed), so no token fields are returned.

expires_at.description:
Unix-seconds access-token expiry, present only on the auto-login path
(existing user with a password). Lets the client schedule a proactive
refresh instead of waiting for the first 401; the signup path omits it.

signup_token.description:
Short-lived JWT token for completing signup (30 min expiry).
Only present for users who haven't set a password yet.
